name: What information should I gather before getting an older-home renovation estimate?

mainEntity.name: What information should I gather before getting an older-home renovation estimate?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before approving a design, collect the home’s age, available plans, prior permits, inspection reports, utility records, and any evidence of previous additions or conversions. Context: for older properties, missing documentation can make field verification especially important; Elite Remodeling & Design can develop a plan around existing conditions and intended use. Key factors: accurate dimensions, service-panel capacity, plumbing routes, roof and drainage conditions, and whether rooms were altered without clear records. Practical guidance: photograph ceilings, crawl spaces, attic areas, panels, water heaters, and visible damage. Tell the design team about leaks, odors, cracks, recurring electrical trips, and past repairs. Better information supports a more realistic scope.
acceptedAnswer.description: Gather the home’s age, plans, prior permits, inspection reports, utility records, photos, and details about leaks, cracks, electrical issues, or past additions. Include attic, crawl-space, panel, water-heater, roof, and drainage photos so the initial scope reflects more than the finished rooms.
